summary: Iso Kern is a philosopher and scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at KU Leuven, University of Freiburg, Heidelberg University, and National Taiwan University. His posts include the Husserl Archives, Heidelberg University, and the University of Bern.
Issaien Ikeyama is a Buddhist studies scholar. In 1976, he was attested as a professor at both International Buddhist University Junior College and Eizan Gakuin.
Issei Suzuki (1863–1943) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Rissho University, where he also served as a professor.
Issei Yamakawa is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Sophia University and completed a master's course at Aichi Gakuin University.
Itsuko Nishikawa is a linguist and Japanologist who studied at Teachers College, Columbia University. She has served as a Teaching Professor at the University of Washington (attested 2026).
Itsuo Asako is a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He served at Hanazono University as an assistant professor (attested 1997) and professor emeritus (attested 2026).

Ivan Minayev (1840–1890) was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University from circa 1858 to 1862. He held a post at the university's Faculty of Oriental Studies from circa 1871 to 1890.

Ivan Pavlovich Minaev (1840–1890) was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev and Albrecht Weber (1863), and later served as a professor at Saint Petersburg State University.

Ives Goddard (1941–2025) was a linguist who studied at Harvard College (~1959–1963) and Harvard University (~1963–1969). He held posts at Harvard University (~1966–1975), the Smithsonian Institution (~1976), and the National Museum of Natural History (~1976).
Ives Waldo is a scholar of philosophy, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Oxford and studied under Chögyam Trungpa between 1970 and 1988.

Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Harvard University in 2003 under Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, Charles Hallisey, and Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and held a fellowship at Grinnell College.
Ivo Fišer (1929–2004) was an Indologist. He held posts as a lecturer at Charles University (attested 1960) and at the University of Copenhagen's Institute for Indian Philology (attested 1970).

Iwao Ishikawa is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He was a researcher at Toho Kenkyukai (attested 2000) and has held lecturer and researcher roles at ICPBS, IIBS, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).
Iwao Nakajima studied at Hitotsubashi University and under Nichiki Kimura. He held posts at the NHK Broadcasting Culture Research Institute until 1975 and at Sandhaan (attested 1999).
Iwao Shima (1950–2007) was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at Nagoya University (~1969–1978) and served at Kanazawa University from circa 1989 to 2007, becoming a professor circa 1999.

Izumi Hoshi is a Tibetologist and linguist who completed her degrees at the University of Tokyo between ~1987 and 1997. She joined the Tokyo University of Foreign Studies as an assistant professor in 1997 and served as director from 2019 to 2023.
Izumi Matsuda-Kiami is a linguist and Japanologist who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. She has served as a Teaching Professor at the University of Washington (attested 2026).

J. A. B. van Buitenen (1928–1979) was an Indologist and philosopher. He earned his doctorate under Jan Gonda at Utrecht University, worked at Deccan College, taught at Utrecht University, and became Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Chicago.
J. B. Disanayaka is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Colombo from circa 1982 to 2002 and was attested at SOAS University of London in 1996.

J. Gordon Melton is a religious studies scholar educated at Birmingham-Southern College, Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary, and Northwestern University. He founded the Institute for the Study of American Religion and held posts at UC Santa Barbara and Baylor University.
